items.title: Allow servers to advertise lack of RFC 8707 resource indicator support
items.excerpt: Some authorization servers, such as Microsoft Entra ID, do not support RFC 8707 resource indicators and reject authorization and token requests that include the resource parameter (AADSTS901002). Removing the parameter unilaterally on the client is not acceptable: the MCP specification requires it, and it binds the token audience, so omitting it silently opens a token theft window against servers that do support it.

items.title: fix(core): enforce maxTotalTimeout as a hard cap
items.excerpt: Fixes #2695. `maxTotalTimeout` is documented as a hard cap, but `_setupTimeout` armed the pending timer with `timeout` only. When a request's fiber is dropped while it waits for the server, e.g. a `2026-07-28` handler asked the client for input and the `input_required` answer ended the request, and the handler throws while it unwinds (in a `finally`), `HandlerFiberState::threw()` kept the throwable for a rethrow that never comes: the failure was lost without a trace. `HandlerFibers::step()` now marks the state while the

items.title: [Server] Read only new entries when polling `InMemoryNotificationBus`
items.excerpt: `InMemoryNotificationBus::since()` walked its whole backlog on every poll, so each caught-up `subscriptions/listen` stream paid for every entry kept. Sequences have no gaps, so it now reads from the cursor only, and hands the backlog back in one go to a reader that fell behind it. On PHP 8.5, a caught-up poll drops from 2.9 µs to 0.07 µs with the default backlog of 256, and from 114 µs to 0.07 µs with 10,000 entries.
